newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa may run for Congress.
newsitem.headline: Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa may run for Congress.

text.p: Popular Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa may run for Congress this year on a slate expected to be headed by former President Raul Alfonsin of the Radical Party, local newspapers said on Thursday.
Sosa will take part in the Radical campaign in Buenos Aires province "either as a candidate or through an active endorsement of the party list," a spokesman for Alfonsin told the daily Clarin.

La Nacion newspaper ran a similar story about Sosa, a native of the northern province of Tucuman whose deep, powerful vocals and versions of popular folk songs like "Gracias a la vida" (Thanks to Life) have won her a huge following in Latin America and beyond.

If she decides to run for a seat in the Lower House of Congress in October's mid-term elections, Sosa was expected to clinch the third slot on Alfonsin's list. The Radicals will vie with centre-left coalition Frepaso for liberal votes in the province, the country's largest electoral district that has traditionally been the stronghold of the ruling Peronist party.
Sosa is an outspoken supporter of Alfonsin, who was elected president in 1983 and steered Argentina to democracy after six years of military dictorship.
